gettingStarted.availability.pending: Version {version} of {name} is not on npm yet: its publication is pending. The command below will work once it is published.
gettingStarted.availability.title: Package availability
gettingStarted.component.body: Start with a simple action. FormaProvider is optional in an application in English: it replaces the few texts that the components show on their own.
gettingStarted.component.title: Compose your first component
gettingStarted.foundations.body: Import the three stylesheets once, in the entry point of your application and before your own CSS: the tokens first, then the rules of the components, then the base utilities.
gettingStarted.foundations.roles: Then ask for a color or a space by its role, not by its value. Forma UI does not bundle the font: --font-family lists Inter Variable and Inter, so load one of them.
gettingStarted.foundations.title: Apply the foundations
gettingStarted.lead: Connect Forma UI to your project and build your first screen.
gettingStarted.next.body: Compare the variants of each component and read its sizes, states and accessibility.
gettingStarted.next.title: Explore the components
gettingStarted.package.body: Install the package with React and React DOM, its peer dependencies (^19.2): the package never bundles its own copy of React.
gettingStarted.package.title: Connect the library
gettingStarted.theme.body: Offer light, dark and system. The store keeps the preference, and themeScript applies it before the first paint: it has to be in the HTML that is served, because a script that React renders does not run.
gettingStarted.theme.title: Respect the theme preference
gettingStarted.theme.try: Try it: this control writes the same store as the theme switcher of the top bar.
gettingStarted.verify.body: Review the controls in context before you build more screens.
gettingStarted.verify.keyboard: Keyboard: reach every action and see where the focus is.
gettingStarted.verify.responsive: Responsive: check a phone and the widths in between.
gettingStarted.verify.states: States: check loading, errors, disabled and read-only.
gettingStarted.verify.themes: Themes: check that it reads well in light, dark and system.
gettingStarted.verify.title: Check the experience
